name: Primoris
founded: 1960 (operating heritage via ARB Inc., California; public July 2008 via merger with blank-check company Rhapsody Acquisition Corp.)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Primoris is the AI buildout's 'outside-the-walls' contractor caught in a self-inflicted 2026 credibility crisis. The Dallas specialty contractor — #4 US solar contractor (3.22 GW installed in 2025, Solar Power World), a top-10 specialty firm with gas-generation EPC, T&D, and fiber capability — sells exactly what AI campuses need around the building: behind-the-meter gas power (a West Texas off-grid plant with Crusoe), utility infrastructure and duct banks (Meta Nebraska, $250M+; Northern Virginia), and, via the $422M PayneCrest acquisition (May 2026), inside-the-fence electrical distribution. But 2026 broke a two-year beat streak: after FY2025 revenue of $7.6B (+19%) and beats in all eight 2024-25 quarters, cost overruns on six renewables projects forced guidance cuts in May and June that slashed adjusted EPS ~57% (to $2.05-2.60 from $5.80-6.00 initial), the COO and Renewables president departed, the stock fell ~62% from its $205.50 high (market cap now ~$4.15B), and a securities class action (class period 2025-08-05 to 2026-06-22) is active. The counterweight: a record $13.9B backlog at June 30, 2026 ($8.2B MSA), $2.0B of Q2 Energy awards tied to power and data-center growth, and a new CEO (Koti Vadlamudi, 30-year Jacobs veteran, since November 2025) resetting project controls. Q3 2026 results expected ~November 2 (unconfirmed).
ecosystemRole: The energy-infrastructure specialty contractor of the AI buildout's perimeter: utility-scale solar and BESS EPC, behind-the-meter gas generation, transmission/substations, duct banks, and fiber — everything that powers and connects a data center, sold to utilities, hyperscalers, and neocloud developers.

productsAndServices.name: Energy Segment — Renewables, Gas Generation & Industrial EPC
productsAndServices.description: FY2025 revenue $5.0B. Utility-scale solar and battery-storage EPC (#4 US solar contractor, 3.22 GW installed in 2025), full EPC of natural-gas-fired generation including behind-the-meter and microgrid plants, industrial construction, heavy civil, pipeline services, and engineering. Renewables revenue ran $3.0B in 2025 but is guided down to ~$2.1B in 2026 after cost overruns on six projects forced a selectivity reset.
highlights: West-Central Texas off-grid natural-gas power plant with Crusoe — dedicated AI-data-center power, the marquee behind-the-meter credential
$2.0B of new Energy-segment awards in Q2 2026 across gas generation, industrial construction, and electric services 'supporting power and data center growth'
Solar Power World #4 US solar contractor 2026 (3.22 GW in 2025); top-5 in the 2025 list (2.9 GW in 2024); Premier PV O&M/repowering unit at $55M backlog
Energy backlog $6.2B at June 30, 2026 ($3.5B fixed next-12-month)
productsAndServices.positioning: One of the few contractors selling both sides of the AI-power equation — renewables-plus-storage AND gas generation — though the 2026 renewables overruns show the fixed-price EPC slice carries the portfolio's execution risk. Peer set: SOLV, Mortenson, Blattner (Quanta), MasTec Clean Energy on solar; gas-EPC competition from Kiewit and the OEM-aligned builders.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Fixed-price and unit-price EPC contracts with IPPs, utilities, and data-center power developers; fixed-price is <15% of the total company portfolio
productsAndServices.roadmap: 2026 renewables reset under interim leadership; gas-generation and data-center-adjacent awards driving the record backlog

productsAndServices.name: Utilities Segment — Power Delivery, Gas Operations & Communications
productsAndServices.category: Utility T&D, gas distribution, and fiber construction
productsAndServices.description: FY2025 revenue $2.7B. Recurring, MSA-heavy utility services: electric transmission and distribution and substations (Power Delivery), natural-gas utility distribution (Gas Operations), and fiber/telecom network construction (Communications). The segment is the margin-stability anchor — H2 2026 target gross margins of 10-12% versus 6-8% for Energy.
highlights: Utilities backlog $7.7B at June 30, 2026; company-wide MSA backlog $8.2B of the $13.9B total — the recurring-revenue base
Margin-expansion driver in Q1 2026 even as renewables deteriorated
Duct-bank and manhole construction for data centers via R.B. Hinkle (Virginia): 11,000 linear ft of duct banks, 59 manholes on the IAD 350 Data Center
productsAndServices.positioning: The stable two-thirds of the story: master-service-agreement work with utilities whose load growth is now driven by data-center interconnection — competing with Quanta, MasTec, and MYR Group at smaller scale
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Multi-year MSAs and unit-price contracts with electric, gas, and telecom utilities
productsAndServices.roadmap: Rate-base-funded T&D growth as utilities build for data-center load

productsAndServices.name: Data-Center Services Bundle (cross-segment)
productsAndServices.description: Primoris packages itself as 'the premier partner for powering data centers' — planning, building, and connecting natural gas, solar-plus-BESS, and power-delivery infrastructure, deliberately focused 'outside the walls': site preparation, gas power generation, utility infrastructure (T&D, substations, duct banks), medium-voltage and critical/rack power distribution, and fiber network construction. The May 2026 PayneCrest acquisition extends the bundle inside the fence.
highlights: Meta Nebraska: three data-center facilities, $250M+ in contracts (utilities, telecom duct banks, MV/600V distribution)
Crusoe West Texas off-grid gas plant; IAD 350 Virginia duct-bank scope
~$1.7B of potential data-center projects cited in the 2025 pipeline (management commentary via third-party relay)
PayneCrest Electric ($422M announced; ~$399.5M at close): St. Louis electrical contractor, 600+ employees, 2026E revenue $350-370M, adj EBITDA $38-42M — explicit data-center-services rationale
productsAndServices.positioning: Complements rather than competes with the building GCs (Turner, DPR, HITT build the shells; Primoris powers and connects them) — the same lane Quanta and MasTec are racing into with far larger balance sheets
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct contracts with hyperscalers and developers plus utility MSAs serving data-center load
productsAndServices.roadmap: PayneCrest integration; converting the data-center pipeline into backlog under the new CEO's project-controls regime

strategyRead: 1. (High confidence) We assess 2026 transformed Primoris's investment identity from momentum compounder to execution-credibility turnaround: eight consecutive beats through FY2024-25 gave way to two guidance cuts in seven weeks (cumulative ~57% off adjusted EPS), a COO and segment-president exit, and an active securities class action. The record $13.9B backlog and $2.0B of Q2 awards show demand intact — the doubt is entirely about whether the company can price and control fixed-price renewables work.

2. (High confidence) We assess the data-center strategy is deliberately perimeter-focused and real: named Meta Nebraska contracts ($250M+), the Crusoe off-grid gas plant, Virginia duct-bank scope, and the PayneCrest acquisition together give Primoris the most complete 'outside-the-walls' bundle among mid-cap specialty contractors — gas generation, T&D, duct bank, fiber, and now inside-the-fence electrical. It complements the building GCs rather than competing with them.

3. (Moderate confidence) We assess the overrun cluster is a renewables-EPC-specific control failure, not a company-wide one: the Utilities segment expanded margins through the same period, fixed-price work is under 15% of the total portfolio, and the six problem projects sit in exactly the slice (utility-scale solar EPC) where weather, labor productivity, and redesigns concentrate. That makes the fix organizational (estimating and cost-to-complete discipline) rather than structural — consistent with hiring a Jacobs-trained CEO.

4. (Moderate confidence) We assess the gas-generation franchise is quietly becoming the more valuable AI asset: behind-the-meter gas for AI campuses (Crusoe) has none of the renewables segment's IRA/tariff/interconnection policy exposure, and Q2 2026's $2.0B award flow leaned into gas generation and electric services. If renewables stays reset at ~$2.1B/yr, the mix shift does the de-risking on its own.

5. (Moderate confidence) We assess the balance-sheet sequencing was unlucky bordering on undisciplined: ~$400M borrowed for PayneCrest and $50M of buybacks executed at an average $111.29 — weeks before disclosures that took the stock to $77. Liquidity remains adequate ($958.9M total), but capital-allocation credibility is now bundled into the same repair job as project controls.

6. (Low confidence) We assess consensus (Buy, ~$120 average target — 55% above the price) is pricing a successful FY2027 normalization (~$4.79 consensus EPS, ~16x forward). That is plausible on the backlog but assumes no adverse class-action development and no third overrun disclosure; either would reset the multiple again. Q3 2026 results (~November 2, unconfirmed) are the next test.
